Thanks again for taking the time today — quick recap from our discovery and next steps on the audit-logs/evidence items you requested.

4) Schedule a short tech validation call (30 min) to review the sample and access controls — you suggested Jun 16.

I'll attach the Redwood audit-logs data dictionary for reference and follow up with the sample export once I have it.

Marissa — thanks for the notes. A few clarifications and the specific evidence items we need to validate for our security and compliance teams:

Required items:
- Log fields: for each access event, we need user identity (user_id or email), API key or service account id, request_id, resource_id, action (read/write/export), timestamp (UTC), source IP, region/availability zone, model_version, and a pointer to the request/response payload (or hash).
- Filtered exports: sample export covering 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-07 filtered to events touching PII buckets.
- Export formats: Parquet preferred; CSV acceptable if Parquet cannot be produced quickly.
- Integrity proof: cryptographic hash of exported file(s) and a statement of who (Redwood personnel) had access to the export.
- Retention: we must understand your default retention for hosted endpoints and whether you can store / escrow audit logs for 7 years. If Redwood cannot retain 7 years in hosted mode, can we route logs to a customer-owned S3 for long-term retention?
- Access controls: list of Redwood roles that can view raw logs; SSO/KMS integration for Private deployments; whether exports require an internal approval workflow.

Timeline: could you provide the sample export and a short write-up of retention options by EOD Tue, Jun 15? We can then confirm the tech validation call for Jun 16. I've attached our internal evidence request form for reference.

Thanks,
Sandeep Rao
Head of Cloud Security — FinCoBank
sandeep.rao@fincobank.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: FinCoBank — audit logs / data access qualification

Marissa / team — quick technical answers and proposed deliverables. Happy to join the validation call.

1) Export formats & fields
- We can produce exports in Parquet or CSV. Parquet is preferred for schema preservation and performance.
- Default fields included: timestamp_utc, request_id, user_id, user_email, service_account_id, api_key_id (redacted partial), resource_id, action_type (read/write/export), model_version, request_hash, response_hash, source_ip, region, instance_id, latency_ms.
- PII-sensitive fields (payloads) are not included in default exports; we can include a pointer/hash to the payload and provide a separate, scoped export if requested and allowed by config.

2) Retention and residency
- Hosted (Redwood API): default audit-log retention = 90 days. We do not retain 7 years in hosted mode by default.
- Dedicated/Private: retention is configurable. For Private deployments we can configure retention to meet 7-year requirements and optionally export/append logs to a customer-owned S3 bucket in us-east-1.
- For FinCoBank, the recommended approach for 7-year retention is to set up a Dedicated or Private deployment and configure automated archival to your S3 (we can help with the setup).

3) Integrity & evidence
- We can provide exported files with a SHA-256 manifest and signed manifest (signed by Redwood key). We can also produce an audit bundle that includes export hashes, RedTeam access logs for the export operation, and a short chain-of-custody statement.

4) Access controls & approvals
- Internal roles that can view raw audit logs are limited to: infra_sre, security_ops, and a restricted subset of platform_engineers; access is logged and requires 2FA and SSO.
- Exports require an internal ticket and approval (security_ops) for hosted customers; for Private deployments, exports can be configured to require customer-managed approval via an API call.

Deliverables we'll provide by Tue EOD Jun 15:
- Sample export (CSV + Parquet) for 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-07 filtered to PII-touching events. (attachment: audit_log_sample_20260601-20260607.csv)
- Export process overview (PDF) describing delivery options (signed S3, pre-signed URLs, console download) and integrity proof. (attachment: export_process_overview.pdf)
- Data dictionary (already attached by Marissa) and a short note on roles with access.

If we need to accelerate the Private/Dedicated setup for archival, let's surface cost implications — Jordan, can you take point on pricing?

—Aditya

Attachments: audit_log_sample_20260601-20260607.csv, export_process_overview.pdf
